title: A tiny event system
description:
Let parts of a program react to events by registering functions.

```
on("score", ...) twice
emit("score", 10) -> "+10 points" and "total 10"
emit("score", 5)  -> "+5 points" and "total 15"
off(first listener); emit("score", 1) -> "total 16"
```

starter.main.lua:
local listeners = {}
local next_id = 1

local function on(name, fn)
  return 0
end

local function emit(name, ...)
end

local total = 0
on("score", function(n) print("+" .. n .. " points") end)
on("score", function(n) total = total + n print("total " .. total) end)
emit("score", 10)

hints: `listeners[name]` is a list of `{ id = ..., fn = ... }`; `off` searches every list for the id and `table.remove`s it (lesson 3.05).
Passing `...` straight on, `entry.fn(...)`, forwards every argument.
requirements: `on(name, fn)` adds a listener and returns an id; `off(id)` removes it.
`emit(name, ...)` calls every listener of that event in the order they were added, with the extra arguments.
Keep everything in local tables; no globals.
stretch: Add `once(name, fn)` that removes itself after running.
